transcriptText:
Two cards. Only you get to see them. And that's where every hand of poker begins. So let's not talk about it... let's play one. Right now. I'll tell you what you need, the moment you need it.

This is Ada. She has two cards too... but you can't see hers. The chips in the middle are the pot. That's what you're playing for. Every time it's your turn, you get three choices. Fold, and you're out. Call, and you match the bet. Raise, and you make it bigger. For now... call.

Now the shared cards. Three come out at once. That's the flop... and they belong to both of you. Look what you've got. King, queen, jack, ten. One more card in a row, and that's a straight. Ada bets. Stay in... call.

One more card. The turn. Nothing for either of you, so you both check... that just means passing, with no bet. And the last card... the river. Nine. King down to nine... that's your straight. This time, you bet.

Cards up. Ada has ace-jack. A pair of jacks. Your straight beats it, and the pot is yours. Best five cards wins. But here's the secret... you don't always need the best hand. Bet, and if everyone else folds, the pot is yours, without showing a thing.

So... what decides who wins? In one hand, the cards. Ada could just as easily have hit. But over hundreds of hands... the better decisions take the chips. That's what you'll learn here, one decision at a time. Up next: luck and skill.
